mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% and 20-day forward returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: An annualized 12-month CPI change exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL 12m change > 3.0%) signals inflation-driven monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL 12m change > 3.0% and 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS > 12m avg) and housing starts (HOUST > 12m avg) signal robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS > 12m avg and HOUST > 12m avg and 20-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6.0%), a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE 3m change < 0) indicates economic recovery, increasing corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 6.0% and UNRATE 3m change < 0 and 20-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1500 units (HOUST > 1500) reflect strong consumer demand for residential construction, a leading indicator of economic growth that produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500 and 20-day forward returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) indicates contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate revenue growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 and 20-day forward returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of sub-0.5% interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals aggressive monetary stimulus for economic recovery, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.0% and 20-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rising interest rates increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and 60-day forward returns are positive.
